items.note: Children do a standardized drawing task with a social robot that gives either pre-recorded generic compliments or contextualized feedback from a vision-language model, and the value of the creative product is scored; the comparison is one robot configuration against another, N=49 is just under the 50 threshold, and assignment is not described.

Lab experiment (2x2) in which participants brainstorm alone or with GenAI help while anticipating a human or AI teammate, with idea quantity, quality, flexibility, and originality scored; the abstract does not state random assignment.

Meta-analysis of 17 studies (115 effect sizes) comparing human ideas with GenAI-prompted ideas, finding a small non-significant pooled effect favoring GenAI; it covers AI vs human output, not co-creation, and has PsyArXiv and MIC 2025 abstract versions.

Systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 19 studies (61 effect sizes) on homogenization of creative output in human-AI co-creation, finding a small significant homogenization effect; same work as the ECCE 2026 short paper and the PsyArXiv preprint, and its included-study list is a source for further candidates.

Analyzes over six million text-to-image prompts on CivitAI over seven months and finds prompt language homogenizes as participation grows, with lexical prompt similarity correlating with visual similarity (Vendi scores) of generated images; no human-without-AI comparison.

Preregistered BCG field experiment randomly assigning 758 consultants to no AI, GPT-4, or GPT-4 plus prompt overview on 18 tasks including creative product ideation, with quality scored; the idea-diversity result appears in the 2023 SSRN working paper (HBS WP 24-013), not in the abstract.

Preregistered field experiment at Procter & Gamble randomly assigning 791 professionals to AI or no AI, alone or in two-person teams, on real product innovation challenges, with solution quality scored; NBER WP 33641 reports N=776 for the same study.

Within-subject study (N=37) comparing an unmodified Llama model, a concept-suppressed version, and apparently unaided ideation on a conceptual ideation challenge; the abstract reports only workload and ownership ratings plus qualitative analysis, so it may be self-report only and is below 50 participants.

Preregistered metaphor-writing experiment with native and non-native English writers in three arms (no AI, AI ideation, AI refinement) measuring collective diversity and rated quality, plus an LLM-persona simulation of the writer pool; abstract from OpenAlex and the arXiv page, N and assignment method not stated.

Compares ideas from AI-based ideation with ideas from an expert workshop at BSH on sustainable packaging, rated on novelty, value, and feasibility; likely AI vs human output (context_ai_vs_human), but the abstract leaves unclear whether people ran the AI-based ideation and Holzner et al. 2025 also code it as people with vs without AI, so full text should decide.
